"@USER A9.3: Our experts created a spectrum of policy options to expand and improve #Medicaid & #CHIP coverage so every kid has the health care coverage they need. #WellnessWed ✅Evidence to Action brief HTTPURL    ✅Policy solutions HTTPURL"

"@USER A9.2: Policymakers can help to remove the "unwelcome mat" created by cuts to enrollment assistance & exacerbated by policies like the #publiccharge rule. By boosting outreach efforts, we can help more families access much-needed #CHIP & #Medicaid benefits. #WellnessWed"

"@USER A9.1: States can enhance opportunities for employers & families to buy-in to #CHIP coverage. PA allows families to buy-in to coverage which gives kids to access more robust pediatric benefits than they are likely to get from private insurance. #WellnessWed"

"@USER A8.2: Our research from the 2008 recession tells us there was an increase in childrens enrollment in public programs following families loss of employer sponsored insurance. We anticipate similar patterns as families face similar hardships. #WellnessWed"

"@USER A8.1: We expect enrollment in both #CHIP & #Medicaid to increase as a result of #COVID19 as people lose employer sponsored insurance or become newly eligible as their income dips. #WellnessWed"
"@USER A7.3: To ensure that families dont have to worry about losing coverage, policymakers should also consider making #CHIP funding permanent at the federal level.  #WellnessWed"

"@USER A7.2: States w/ lower income eligibility levels account for a disproportionate # of uninsured children & these numbers are growing. States w/ upper eligibility levels below national median could consider raising eligibility levels to the national median, at least. #WellnessWed"

"@USER A7.1: Given that 57% of uninsured children in 2017 were eligible for but not enrolled in #Medicaid or #CHIP, policymakers should consider increasing the ease with which families can sign up, maintain & renew their coverage. #WellnessWed"
"@USER A6.2: #CHIP & #Medicaid work together & have helped us achieve near universal coverage for children over the past decade. In some states theyre run as an integrated program. #WellnessWed"

"@USER A6.1: #CHIP serves those whose income puts them above the threshold for #Medicaid, but who may not have access to employer-sponsored insurance or for whom private insurance is too expensive. #WellnessWed"

"@USER A5.2: #CHIP benefits are generally comprehensive but they vary by state.  State eligibility levels range from family income of 170% to 400% FPL, but are at or above 200% FPL in most states. #WellnessWed"

"@USER A5.1: States can run their CHIP programs separate from their Medicaid programs, as an expansion of their Medicaid program, or a combination of the two. PA runs a separate CHIP program. #WellnessWed"

"@USER A4.2: Studies show that kids with #CHIP coverage are more likely to graduate high school & enroll in college. Research also indicates that these kids are less likely to have chronic conditions as adults. #WellnessWed"
"@USER A4.1: #CHIP increases access to care that helps kids become healthy & productive as they grow, while also providing important financial protection to families. #WellnessWed"

"@USER A3: Yes, but as a state-run program, states can choose to run #CHIP in different ways. PAs CHIP program, created in 1993, would later serve as a model for the federal CHIP program. #WellnessWed"
"@USER A2.2: In PA, families can visit HTTPURL to apply for or renew coverage. #WellnessWed"

"@USER A2.1: Together with #Medicaid, #CHIP has contributed to a steady decline in uninsurance rates among children for the past decade. Together they covered nearly 40% of all kids in 2018. #WellnessWed"
"@USER A1: #CHIP has been providing kids with low-cost or no-cost health insurance since 1997 (1993 in PA!), providing vital support to families for over 2 decades. #WellnessWed"
